title: When Should We Stop a Pilot?
scene: Your team has been testing a new service for several weeks. The results are weaker than expected, but some members want to continue.
sceneJa: 新サービスの試行結果が目標に届かない中、過去の投資にとらわれず、追加検証によって有益な根拠が得られるかを判断する場面。

chunks.en: When a pilot fails to meet its targets,
chunks.ja: 試験的な取り組みが目標を達成できなかったとき
チームはつい〜したくなるかもしれません
そのまま続けることを

chunks.en: the time and money already spent
chunks.ja: すでに費やした時間とお金が
決めるべきではありません
私たちは問う必要があります
そのテストを継続することが
生み出す見込みがあるかどうかを
もし答えが「いいえ」なら
試験的な取り組みを中止することが

chunks.en: may be the most reasonable decision.
chunks.ja: 最も合理的な判断かもしれません

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: the time and money already spent / should not determine / what we do next
the time / and money already / spent should / not determine what
the time and / money already spent should / not determine what we / do next
questions.explanation: Keep the complete subject, its verb phrase, and the object clause as meaningful units.

questions.question: What does ‘be tempted to keep going’ mean?
options: Feel a strong desire to continue, even if it may not be wise.
questions.explanation: ‘Be tempted to’ means to feel drawn toward an action that may not be wise.

questions.question: What should determine whether the team continues?
options: How much money has already been spent.
How long the team has worked on the project.
Whether continuing is likely to produce useful new evidence.
questions.explanation: The decision should focus on the expected value of further learning, not sunk costs.

speak: Read ‘The time and money already spent / should not determine / what we do next’ three times. First slowly, then stress ‘already spent’, and finally stress ‘what we do next’. Finish with ‘If the answer is no, / stopping the pilot / may be the most reasonable decision’ in a calm, objective tone.
review: Previous lesson: ‘under different conditions’, ‘justify further investment’, and ‘meet the criteria’. Yesterday we asked what evidence would justify scaling up; today we ask what evidence would justify continuing, separating past investment from the future value of another test.
